question: Globalisation, by connecting countries, shall result in ________.

options.text: no change in competition among producers

solution:
The correct answer is __**greater competition among producers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Globalisation leads to a global market where producers from different countries compete, thereby increasing competition. (Source: World Bank)
 
• Increased competition often results in better products and services as producers strive to innovate and improve quality. (Source: International Monetary Fund)
 
• Consumers benefit from lower prices and a wider variety of goods and services due to heightened competition. (Source: OECD)
 
• Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face significant challenges but also opportunities to expand their markets internationally. (Source: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Globalisation:**

 
 
• The process of interaction and integration among people, companies, and governments worldwide, driven by international trade and investment and aided by information technology.
 
• It leads to economic growth, cultural exchange, and technological advancements. (Source: World Trade Organization)
 
 
 
• **Market Competition:**
 
 
• The rivalry among sellers trying to achieve goals such as increasing profits, market share, and sales volume by varying the elements of the marketing mix: price, product, distribution, and promotion.
 
• Heightened competition can drive innovation and efficiency. (Source: Harvard Business Review)
 
 
 
• **Trade Liberalization:**
 
 
• The removal or reduction of restrictions or barriers on the free exchange of goods between nations, including tariffs, duties, and quotas.
 
• It is a key component of globalisation that facilitates greater competition. (Source: World Economic Forum)
 
 
 
• **Economic Integration:**
 
 
• Where countries coordinate their economic policies to reduce trade barriers and increase economic cooperation.
 
• Examples include the European Union (EU) and the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA). (Source: European Commission)
